name: Pippalyadi Lauha

sections.overview:
Pippalyadi Lauha – Ingredients, Preparation, Medicinal Properties, Indications Dosage 
 REFERENCE – A.F.I. Part 1 – 21:3 (Bhaisajya Ratnavali, Hikkasvasadhikara verse 61) 
 Abstract 
 Modern lifestyles, fueled by gadgets, science, and technology, have intensified health challenges through poor diet, injuries, rising mental stress, inadequate hygiene, and unhealthy habits. True health demands balance across mental, physical, and spiritual realms. But today’s stressful urban lifestyles, marked by environmental pollution and population growth, respiratory disorders like Shwasa Roga (labored breathing akin to asthma) and Hikka (hiccups) are rising across all ages, with common symptoms of breathlessness, cough, and interrupted breathing due to Vata-Kapha imbalances. Classical Ayurvedic texts highlight Shwasa’s cardinal feature of shwasa krichra (difficulty breathing) and Hikka’s spasmodic diaphragmatic interruptions triggered by modern factors like stress and cold exposure. Proper inhalation delivers vital oxygen and prana to cells, underscoring the need for early dosha-specific interventions to restore pranavaha srotas (breathing channels) balance and prevent chronicity. For this Pippalyadi Lauha is one of the best herbomineral formulations of Ayurveda to bring this balance. Let’s explore this formulation in detail.
sections.introduction:
Pippalyadi Lauha is a classical herbo-mineral Ayurvedic formulation detailed in Bhaishajya Ratnavali’s Hikka–Shwasa Adhikara (Chapter on Hiccup and Dyspnea). This potent remedy blends equal parts of Pippali ( Piper longum ) along with 7 other ingredients and 8 parts of Lauha Bhasma (incinerated iron) for enhanced efficacy. It helps in restoring the udana vayu (a vital subtype of Vata Dosha, governs upward and outward bodily movements, including speech and breathing) disturbance. That in turn ignites weak digestive fire (Agnimandya), relieves vomiting (Chardi), hiccups (Hikka), dyspnea/asthma (Shwasa), and low-grade fever (Mandajvara). 
 …हन्ति सुदारुणम्।। ६१।। (Bhaisajya Ratnavali, Hikkasvasadhikara verse 61) 
 So the part of phrase implies that Pippalyadi Lauha is capable of alleviating even severe and stubborn forms of disease, especially respiratory and digestive conditions. 
 Classical Indication 
 Hikka- shwasa (hiccups and respiratory disorders)
sections.ingredients:
पिप्पल्यामलकीद्राक्षाकोलास्थिमधुशर्कराः । 
 विडङ्गपुष्करेयुक्तं लोहं ……….॥ ६१ ॥ (Bhaisajya Ratnavali, Hikkasvasadhikara verse 61) 

 Pippali fruit ( Piper longum ) – 1 part 
 Amalaki ( Emblica officinalis )- 1 part 
 Draksha dried fruit ( Vitis vinifera )- 1 part 
 Kolasthi ( Ziziphus jujuba )- 1 part 
 Madhu (honey)- 1 part 
 Sharkara (sugar)- 1 part 
 Vidanga fruit ( Embelia ribes )- 1 part 
 Pushkara root ( Inula racemosa )- 1 part 
 Lauha Bhasma (incinerated iron)- 8 parts 


 Ingredient Description 

 Pippali ( Piper longum ) fruit acts as a Kapha-Vata pacifier in Ayurveda, decongesting the lungs, stabilizing Vata to relieve Hiccup spasms, and easing respiratory channels through bronchodilation and expectorant effects. In modern pharmacology, its key compound piperine inhibits bronchospasm, antagonizes histamine release, and reduces airway inflammation, thereby providing anti-asthmatic activity. 
 Amalaki ( Emblica officinalis ) serves as a three dosha pacifying and rejuvenating in Ayurveda, clearing excess mucus from respiratory pathways in Shwasa while soothing irritated channels to control hiccups. Modern studies highlight its high vitamin C content, which boosts mucociliary clearance and immunity, alongside gallic acid that attenuates airway hyperresponsiveness and inflammation in asthma models. 
 Draksha ( Vitis vinifera ) balances Pitta-Kapha doshas, offering demulcent action to soothe the throat in Shwasa and calm Vata-induced spasms during Hiccups. Contemporarily, resveratrol and oligomeric proanthocyanidins (OPCs) exert anti-inflammatory and bronchodilatory effects, while quercetin stabilizes mast cells to modulate histamine-mediated respiratory distress. 
 Kolasthi ( Ziziphus jujuba ) with its Madhura Rasa (sweet taste) and three dosha pacifying properties, supports digestive fire to reduce endotoxin formation that exacerbates Hikka and Shwasa. In modern terms, its saponins provide sedative effects to calm diaphragmatic spasms in hiccups, complemented by flavonoids that soothe respiratory mucosa and aid overall lung comfort. 
 Madhu (Honey) functions as a Lekhana dravya, scraping Kapha from respiratory channels to expel mucus in Shwasa and directly pacify Hiccups. Scientifically, it inhibits pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-4 and IL-5, reduces eosinophil infiltration and mucus hypersecretion in asthma, with flavonoids contributing to its anti-inflammatory and antitussive actions. 
 Sharkara (sugar) possessing Sheeta Virya (cool potency), soothes Pitta-aggravated irritation in the respiratory tract, facilitating relief from Shwasa and Hikka by promoting channel lubrication. Modern perspectives note its hydrating and expectorant support, with trace minerals aiding metabolic processes that indirectly enhance respiratory efficiency. 
 Vidanga ( Embelia ribes ) acts as a potent Kapha pacifier, clearing Ama endotoxins from the lungs to alleviate Shwasa and associated cough in Hiccups conditions. Its christembine alkaloids demonstrate modern bronchial relaxant properties, effectively relieving cough and bronchitis symptoms through antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. 
 Pushkara ( Inula racemosa ) root is renowned as Shwasa-Kasa hara (medicines df, reducing Kapha obstruction and acting as a natural bronchodilator for dyspnea and hiccups. Pharmacologically, alantolactone is the key sesquiterpene that protects against histamine-induced bronchospasm and modulates inflammatory pathways in the airways. 
 Lauha Bhasma (incinerated iron) serves as a Raktaprasadana (blood quality enhancer), correcting anemia that aggravates Shwasa by nourishing blood and supporting Prana flow to vitalize respiration. In contemporary science, its nano-particulate iron enhances oxygen-carrying capacity in hemoglobin, combating hypoxia and fatigue in chronic respiratory disorders. 

 Method Of Preparation 
 Pippalyadi Lauha is prepared as a Lauha Kalpa, a herbo-mineral Ayurvedic formulation where herbal powders are triturated with Lauha Bhasma (calcined iron). All ingredients’ fine powders are taken in equal parts (1 part each), while Lauha Bhasma is taken at 8 parts. These are uniformly mixed in a Khalwa Yantra (mortar-pestle), with Madhu (honey, 1 part) and Sharkara (sugar, 1 part) added gradually during prolonged levigation (Bhavana) for 4-6 hours to achieve a homogenous, semi-solid paste. The mixture is then rolled into small tablets (Vati) of about 250 mg each, shade-dried, and stored in airtight containers. 
 Medicinal Properties 

 For Agnimandya (weak digestive fire) , administer Pippalyadi Lauha (250 mg twice daily) with honey as anupana, rapidly kindling low Agni through deepana (appetizer) action of Pippali-Vidanga synergy, dissolving ama via Lauha Bhasma’s lekhana (scraping) properties, and restoring metabolic harmony by pacifying involved Kapha-Vata doshas. 
 In Chardi (vomiting) due to Pitta-Kapha aggravation with Ajirna (indigestion), Pippalyadi Lauha combines with fresh ginger juice (5 ml), effectively controlling emesis through antiemetic Pushkara-Amalaki effects, anulomana (downward movement) of Vata, and pitta shamaka demulcent action of Draksha-Madhu for gastric soothing and quick recovery. 
 For Hikka (hiccups) from Udana Vayu vitiation and diaphragmatic spasms, Pippalyadi Lauha (250 mg at onset, repeated as needed) with warm honey works optimally, stabilizing prana vayu via bronchodilatory Pippali, spasmolytic Kolasthi-Vidanga, and channel-clearing lekhana synergy to restore pharyngeal-respiratory equilibrium. 
 In Shwasa (dyspnea/asthma) with Kapha-Vata srotorodha (channel obstruction) , administer Pippalyadi Lauha (250 mg twice daily) alongside Sitopaladi Churna (3 g), promoting bronchodilation through Pushkara’s kaphahara (phlegmolytic) potency, expectorant Pippali-Lauha actions, and swasahara (antiasthmatic) herbal-mineral balance for unobstructed pranavaha srotas. 
 For Mandajvara (low-grade fever) of endotoxin-origin with low digestive fire , Pippalyadi Lauha (125-250 mg twice daily) with Triphala juice (10 ml) eradicates mild pyrexia via jvaraghna (antipyretic) Amalaki-Sharkara cooling, ama pachana through Lauha’s deepana, and tridosha shamaka effects to normalize body temperature and prevent chronicity. 

 Impact On Dosha 
 Pippalyadi Lauha primarily balances Kapha-Vata doshas with mild Pitta-pacifying effects through its synergistic ingredients.
sections.indications:
Agnimandya – Weak digestive fire 
 Chardi – Vomiting 
 Hikka – Hiccups 
 Shwasa – Dyspnea / breathlessness / Asthma 
 Mandajvara – Low-grade or mild fever
sections.dosage:
250 mg 
 Anupana (Adjuvant) 
 Honey 
 Contraindication 

 Active peptic ulcers/Gastritis: Avoid in Amla-Pitta or high Pitta conditions with gastric erosion, due to potential irritation from iron and heating herbs. 
 Iron overload disorders (Hemochromatosis) 

 Conclusion 
 Pippalyadi Lauha stands as a time-tested herbo-mineral gem from Bhaishajya Ratnavali, masterfully targeting Kapha-Vata imbalances through synergistic digestive fire kindling, kapha pacifying, and bronchodilatory actions. Its balanced preparation, featuring Pippali’s expectorant potency, Lauha Bhasma’s hematinic scrapping, and soothing property of honey and Vitis ensures rapid digestive fire ignition, respiratory pathways clearance, and dosha equilibrium. This formulation supports respiratory health, anemia correction, and overall vitality through synergistic herbal-mineral action.
